topic: Flipkart Big Billion Days 2026 'Ek Size Bada Le Lo' TV ad by 22feet: why it works

claims.claim: The film is titled 'Ek Size Bada Le Lo' and was conceptualised by 22feet, part of Omnicom Advertising India, for Flipkart's Big Billion Days. It sells large-screen TVs, not clothes.

claims.claim: The film is on Flipkart's official YouTube channel as 'Mummy's vision: 10/10. 🎯 Future-proofing our lives since Day 1! 🔮✨', published 2026-10-03 (08:49 PT), length 80 seconds (1:20). It is not a Short.

sources.title: Mummy's vision: 10/10. Future-proofing our lives since Day 1!

claims.claim: YouTube description, verbatim: "Mummy's “Ek size bada le lo” rule finally paid off—and this time it's not for a school shirt 👕 or shoes 👟! Nervous to pitch a bigger TV to the family? 📺🫣 Her age-old habit (and Flipkart Big Billion Days prices 📉🔥) just solved your wallet anxiety! 💸✨"

sources.title: Mummy's vision: 10/10. Future-proofing our lives since Day 1!

claims.claim: Insight: mothers asking their children to buy clothes one size bigger so they can keep wearing them as they grow. The film carries that into TV shopping: go a size bigger on the screen without a proportionally bigger bill. Coverage describes the tone as humour plus nostalgia, with the film amplified across digital platforms.

claims.claim: Ishan Mehta, Executive Creative Director, 22feet: "The insight of parents buying slightly oversized clothes felt so relatable. The creative unlock was using that mantra, typically reserved for apparels, for a category like large screen TVs."

claims.claim: BBD 2026 is the 13th edition. General sale opened 9 Oct 2026; 24-hour early access from 8 Oct for Plus, VIP/BLACK members and Flipkart cardholders. Flipkart says it has 500M+ registered users, 150M+ products across 80+ categories and 1.4M+ sellers. End date of 18 Oct appears only in deal-aggregator sites, not an official source.

claims.claim: YouTube's public counter showed 8,538,379 views on the Flipkart upload when fetched on 2026-10-19. No trade outlet reported views or engagement. The count likely includes paid pre-roll, so use it as 'over 8.5 million views on YouTube' only, never as organic reach. The like count is hidden or near zero (the page showed 63), which suggests mostly ad-served views.

claims.claim: 'Truth Well Told' is McCann's motto since its founding in 1912: base the ad on a real truth about people and products, then tell it with craft. (Note: McCann is not the agency on this film; it is used here only as a framework.)

sources.title: 'Make something you love': How agencies got their mantras

claims.claim: Research in the Journal of Consumer Research ('Nostalgia Weakens the Desire for Money', Lasaleta, Sedikides and Vohs, 2014, vol. 41 no. 3) found across six experiments that nostalgia reduced people's desire for money and made them willing to pay more for products, through a sense of social connectedness. It is a lab study on willingness to pay, not a test of this ad.

sources.title: Nostalgia Weakens the Desire for Money
